items.title: Volodymyr Zelenskyy says 50,000 North Korean troops will help Russia in war
items.description: The Ukrainian President took to social media to announced that "a decision has been made for 30,000 to 50,000 North Koreans to be deployed on the territory of Russia", while calling on South Korea to provide support for Ukraine's air defence.

items.title: Paramilitary promises footage of supreme leader unseen since March
items.description: Video of Iran's supreme leader Mojtaba Khamenei who has not been seen in public since he assumed the role in March, has been promised by a paramilitary leader.

items.title: Alleged Irish international crime boss extradited from UAE
items.description: 49-year-old Daniel Joseph Kinahan was flown from Dubai to Dublin, the UAE state news agency reported, after his arrest in April, with allegations about his "serious organised crime offences".

items.title: Body found in suitcase in southern NSW
items.description: The body of a person, believed to be female, has been found in a suitcase at Oallen, about 60 kilometres south-east of Goulburn.

items.title: Two airport workers stood down after near miss at Sydney airport
items.description: A Jetstar A320 was forced to brake suddenly to avoid colliding with a Boeing 777 on the tarmac at Sydney Airport, with both planes stopping abruptly in an incident that injured a cabin crew worker.

items.title: The feud between Taylor Swift and Donald Trump just took an unexpected twist
items.description: Despite the enduring animosity towards the pop superstar, the Trump White House and campaign had used several Swift tracks in TikTok videos, before they abruptly disappeared from the president's social media posts.

items.title: Britain's new PM is redefining populist anger
items.description: Britain's new left-leaning PM Andy Burnham has seized the same public discontent driving Nigel Farage on the populist right but with a very different agenda. As One Nation climbs in the polls, Australia should be paying attention.

items.title: Trump is not shy of collecting spoils, and the US presidency has plenty
items.description: The US president's most-recent filings indicate he pocketed more than $US2.2 billion last year through ventures ostensibly run by his family.

items.title: Wildfire forces more than 20,000 people evacuate homes in western Canada
items.description: Thousands of people in British Columbia have been ordered to flee a fast-moving wildfire that nearly doubled in size overnight.

items.title: Raiders bemoan 'f***ing brain explosion' as their season ends
items.description: The Dragons beat the Sharks 24-16 in a thrilling derby victory at Kogarah, as the Knights end the Raiders season with a victory following a "brain explosion" from a key Canberra forward.

items.title: Blues plant one foot in the AFL finals as Saints lose star to hamstring
items.description: Carlton plants one foot in the AFL finals series with a statement victory over the Saints at Docklands.

items.title: Army of volunteers races to save one of Australia's rarest orchids
items.description: It takes years of work, dozens of volunteers, picky pollinators and a special fungus to save Australia’s endangered orchids. Here's why people drive from all over the country to do it anyway.

items.title: Inside this street food market are signs of a crashing currency
items.description: Indonesia's rupiah has fallen to historic lows against the US dollar, causing damage "in most of the economy", analysts say.

items.title: They survived one of our darkest medical scandals, now they want justice
items.description: The 1980s contaminated blood crisis devastated the lives of thousands of Australians who were infected with hepatitis C or HIV. Now, survivor Tristan Stanley, who contracted hep C as a child, has uncovered government documents that raise troubling questions about the scandal.

items.title: Elliot Constable wins Race Around The World
items.description: After 100 days on the road, the winner of Race Around the World has been crowned. Catch up on the final week's films.

items.title: Love story: The grief and relief that comes with the death of your 'big love'
items.description: Hilda Quiroga says she was "struck" by Steve Mayer from the moment they first met until his death at 53 through voluntary assisted dying.

items.title: White chocolate tart with burnt honey and thyme
items.description: This decadent tart has a chocolate and hazelnut crust, no-bake white chocolate and cream cheese filling and is ready in only 30 minutes.

items.title: Parents urged to restrict cow's milk for toddlers
items.description: Paediatricians across Australia are concerned about a jump in iron deficiency in young children due to too much cow's milk, and the need to better educate parents about the issue.

items.title: New Fremantle Traffic Bridge to open ahead of schedule
items.description: The new bridge is set to open before the end of the year, months ahead of schedule, with locals and businesses saying the impact has been better than expected.

items.title: Greens draw firm line on betting perks
items.description: The Greens are not prepared to vote on the government's gambling legislation, outlining some of their main concerns around "predatory" behaviour.

items.title: 'Not good enough': Phone network down for thousands of FNQ residents
items.description: Some residents in remote parts of Far North Queensland have not had telecommunications since Saturday evening, as Telstra works to restore services.

items.title: What we know about Trump's new US ambassador to Australia
items.description: The new US ambassador to Australia, David Brat, says critical minerals, commercial diplomacy and defence cooperation are his top priorities in Canberra.

items.title: 'Mind-blowing' near misses along Adelaide rail lines prompt plea to pedestrians
items.description: Videos captured along Adelaide's suburban train lines of near misses involving pedestrians, including one in which a person dived out of the way at the last moment, have prompted warnings from transport authorities.

items.title: Munster free to play after dangerous contact charge downgraded
items.description: Melbourne Storm five-eighth Cameron Munster avoids suspension after the NRL match review committee downgrades his dangerous contact charge from Saturday's win over Manly.

items.title: Blues start AFLW season with 26-point win over Saints
items.description: Carlton has held off a St Kilda fightback to claim the opening win of the new AFLW season by 26 points in an entertaining game that made a case for more double header fixtures.
